title: Daily physics papers — 4 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking with limited citation evidence for very recent papers, not a measure of readership or downloads.

sections.title: A New Precise Measurement of the e+e- -> pi+pi-(gamma) Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
sections.abstract: The BaBar Collaboration reports a new e+e- -> pi+pi-(gamma) cross-section measurement using 460 fb-1 of initial-state-radiation data and derives its hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to muon g-2.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Full 460 fb-1 sample; a new pion/muon separation using angular distributions; and a precisely reported HVP integral make this the batch's clearest precision-data result for a high-profile observable. The shorter same-day BaBar upload 2611.04596 reports the same measurement and is not counted separately.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give a_mu(pi pi)=525.9±3.5_stat±3.8_syst (10^-10) for the new 2026 measurement over 0.3–1.4 GeV, and 517.8±2.4_stat±3.3_syst when combined with their 2009 result.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 460 fb-1 of on- and off-Upsilon(4S) BaBar data analyzed with initial-state radiation and pion/muon angular distributions
sections.unique_caveat: This is the two-pion contribution over 0.3–1.4 GeV, not a complete muon-g-2 prediction; the paper notes that statistical separation is less precise at the low- and high-energy ends and reports nonzero systematic uncertainty.

sections.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
sections.authors: Aimé Matheron, Michal Šmíd, Felix Karbstein, Sebastian Göde, Willi Hippler et al. (BIREF@HIBEF Collaboration)
sections.abstract: The authors collide an X-ray free-electron-laser probe with an intense optical laser and use dark-field detection and polarimetry to set a low-energy light-by-light-scattering bound substantially below previous laboratory limits.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between high-energy experiment and optics; the EuXFEL/laser experiment reports a low-energy bound about ten orders tighter than earlier experimental limits, while explicitly distinguishing a bound from a detection.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no significant photon excess and set the strongest direct low-energy experimental bound on light-by-light scattering to date, improving previous experimental limits by roughly ten orders of magnitude.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; X-ray free-electron-laser and high-intensity optical-laser collisions at the European XFEL, with dark-field detection and polarimetry
sections.unique_caveat: No light-by-light signal was detected, and the paper says the present setup did not reach the baseline sensitivity needed to detect the QED-predicted signal.

sections.title: Constraints on a Long-Lived X17 Vector Boson with FASER
sections.abstract: Reinterpreting and combining previous FASER dark-photon and axion-like-particle searches as X17 searches, the collaboration finds no excess and excludes a previously unconstrained low-electron-coupling interval.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in experiment and phenomenology; it converts existing Run 3 FASER data into a quantitative new exclusion in an X17 parameter region that had remained open after earlier beam-dump reinterpretations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no excess in 13.6 TeV pp data from 2022 and 2022–2023 searches, excluding 6×10^-5 < epsilon_e < 1.2×10^-4 for the studied 17 MeV protophobic-vector scenario.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; reinterpretation of FASER dark-photon and ALP searches using 13.6 TeV LHC Run 3 data
sections.unique_caveat: The exclusion is conditional on the assumed X17 vector-boson model and couplings; the paper leaves a high-coupling window open, and the X17 itself is not established by this result.

sections.title: Precise and accurate nuclear electric quadrupole moment of 223Ra from molecular spectroscopy
sections.authors: C. M. Fajardo-Zambrano, M. Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, L. Lalanne, J. R. Reilly, O. Ahmad et al.
sections.abstract: Hyperfine-resolved spectroscopy of radioactive 223Ra19F, combined with relativistic coupled-cluster calculations, yields a sub-percent quadrupole-moment determination for 223Ra.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct spectroscopy of a short-lived isotope, threefold better total precision than earlier atomic/ionic determinations, and a reported 0.73% total uncertainty make this a concrete nuclear-structure measurement.
sections.claimed_result: The authors determine Q_s(223Ra)=+1.211(7)_stat(2)_syst(5)_theo eb, with a 0.73% total relative uncertainty.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; hyperfine-resolved collinear resonance-ionization spectroscopy of radioactive RaF, calibrated with relativistic coupled-cluster calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The extracted moment depends on the calculated molecular electric-field gradient; the quoted uncertainty includes a nonzero theoretical component as well as statistical and systematic terms.

sections.title: 3D dark matter map of the JWST COSMOS-Web field using diffusion-based generative priors
sections.authors: Diana Scognamiglio, Brandon Zhao, Katherine L. Bouman, Olivier Doré, Caitlin M. Casey et al.
sections.abstract: A weak-lensing forward model and simulation-trained diffusion prior are used to infer a probabilistic three-dimensional matter map from JWST imaging of the COSMOS-Web field, across 20 lens planes to about z=2.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Combines a major JWST imaging field with a cross-listed machine-learning method; the authors report structures associated with independently identified clusters and posterior uncertainty estimates, rather than a single deterministic map.
sections.claimed_result: The authors reconstruct matter across 20 lens planes in a 0.54 deg^2 field, extending the redshift reach of earlier Hubble-based 3D reconstructions to roughly z=2 and separating some structures that overlap in projection.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST COSMOS-Web imaging analyzed with weak-lensing inference and a diffusion prior trained on cosmological simulations
sections.unique_caveat: This is an inference over one 0.54 deg^2 field, not a direct dark-matter observation; its posterior depends on the forward model and simulation-trained prior.

sections.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
sections.authors: Kai-Xuan Zhang, Beom Hyun Kim, Seungbok Lee, Hao Li, Eugene Park et al.
sections.abstract: High-field Raman spectroscopy finds robust magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3 as temperature rises, with decreasing detuning driving enhanced hybridization near the antiferromagnetic transition.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A measured avoided crossing across temperature, plus cross-listing in materials, optics, and quantum physics, ties a concrete spectroscopy result to a current question about driven magnetic states.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe that magnon-phonon coupling remains robust with warming while the zero-field detuning decreases, enhancing hybridization near the transition temperature.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; high-field Raman spectroscopy of the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed connection to an earlier terahertz-driven metastable state is an interpretation of the coupling data, not a direct demonstration that this mechanism alone explains that state.

sections.title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
sections.authors: Giovanni Adriano, Akilan Rajamani, Francesco Hoch, Farrokh Labib, Nadja Z. Zaouri et al.
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally implement a qubit-efficient quantum-density-functional approach for the ground and first excited states of LiH on a programmable integrated photonic circuit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Experimental photonic-hardware validation of a quantum-chemistry method attracted independent coverage from Quantum Zeitgeist; the paper also reports both ground- and first-excited-state properties.
sections.claimed_result: The authors implement the ensemble extension of VQE for LiH on a quantum-dot single-photon source and integrated circuit, demonstrating their Q-DFT mapping with logarithmic qubit scaling in the number of orbitals.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; LiH calculation on a programmable integrated photonic circuit, compared with noiseless and noisy simulations
sections.unique_caveat: This is a small-molecule proof of implementation, not a demonstration of quantum advantage; finite photon counts and about 89% photon indistinguishability limit accuracy, and the authors note that near-perfect indistinguishability is needed for chemical accuracy.

sections.title: SS 433 Eastern Jet Turbulence Revealed by Spatially-Resolved IXPE Data Analysis
sections.authors: Ningyue Fan, Jack T. Dinsmore, Roger W. Romani
sections.abstract: A spatially resolved reanalysis of 2023 IXPE polarimetry finds that a three-region model better describes the eastern SS 433 jet than a single-zone model, with lower polarization in the sheath.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Uses public IXPE observations and reports a greater-than-3-sigma improvement for spatially resolved regions, adding spatial structure to a high-energy astrophysical polarization analysis; the arXiv comment says submitted to ApJ.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find lower polarization in the jet sheath than in its head and spine, with position angles consistent across regions, and infer enhanced magnetic turbulence at the boundary.
sections.evidence_type: observational; spatially resolved analysis of the 2023 Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) observation of SS 433/W50
sections.unique_caveat: The Kelvin–Helmholtz explanation for the inferred boundary turbulence is tentative; this is a reanalysis of one observation rather than an independent observation.

sections.title: Shallow lunar fractures dominate the long-lasting seismic coda
sections.authors: Lei Zhang, Qian Huang, Minghao Huang, Jinhai Zhang, Dijun Guo
sections.abstract: A fracture-scattering simulation reproduces long lunar seismic codas in Apollo impact records and suggests that fractures in the uppermost kilometre dominate the scattering.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in geophysics and planetary astrophysics; the model is tested against 13 Apollo artificial-impact event–station pairs and reports envelope correlations above 0.9.
sections.claimed_result: The authors propose vacuum fractures as strong seismic-reflection boundaries and find in simulations that fractures in roughly the top 1 km can account for key features of the Apollo coda.
sections.evidence_type: computational; spectral-element simulations compared with Apollo seismic impact records
sections.unique_caveat: Fractures are inferred from a simplified model fit, not directly imaged; results depend on assumed fracture geometry and on the small set of historical impact records.

sections.title: Observation of pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
sections.authors: Chengle Fan, Kaizhou Shi, Xiang Xi, Zhen Gao
sections.abstract: Microwave measurements of gyromagnetic photonic crystals demonstrate pseudospin-selective chiral edge transport and route two channels through multiplexer, demultiplexer, and crossing structures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct near-field and transmission measurements support the claimed unidirectional, pseudospin-selective channels; the authors also report measured crosstalk for a waveguide crossing.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a single chiral edge branch selected by source handedness and average crossing crosstalk of −14.1 and −15.8 dB for the two input channels.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; microwave near-field and transmission measurements on gyromagnetic photonic crystals
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a laboratory photonic-crystal demonstration; its measured channel performance does not establish robustness or scalability in an integrated network.
